subjects.displayTitle: Divine love: the hidden treasure and the life of creation
subjects.introduction: Before anything existed, Bahá’u’lláh says, God knew His love for the human being and therefore created. Love, on this account, is older than the lovers. The tradition of the hidden treasure that longed to be known, the four kinds of love ‘Abdu’l-Bahá describes, and the daring language of God loving His own beauty all belong to a single vision in which creation is an overflow of self-sufficient generosity, not a need. Such language is easily misheard as vanity; here it describes the source from which every lesser love is borrowed, as the sun’s light is lent to the moon. At the same time the Essence praised only by itself exceeds every description we can offer, so that each image remains a pointer. First John moves from the unseen God who is love to the plain duty of loving one another [1], a practical turn that keeps the metaphysics honest. The journey continues toward the love of God as a human response, toward the creation of the world as the fruit of that love, and toward the unknowability of the One who loves.
subjects.arc: Begin with love preceding human existence, explore its relation to divine transcendence and creation, and return to the love that binds a human family.

order.why: Consider the language of God praising His own Essence.
shortened: From eternity Thou didst Thyself describe Thine own Self unto Thy Self, and extol, in Thine own Essence, Thine Essence unto Thine Essence.

order.why: Open with love addressed to the human being before creation.
Introduce the hidden treasure and the desire to be known.
shortened: It is the cause of creation and its manifestation, as expressed in His exalted Word: "I was a hidden treasure and loved to be known, therefore I created creation that I might be known."

order.why: Read love as the key to the treasury of revelation.
Follow love through creation, life, progress, and civilization.
shortened: Know thou of a certainty that Love is the secret of God's holy Dispensation, the manifestation of the All-Merciful, the fountain of spiritual outpourings. Love is heaven's kindly light, the Holy Spirit's eternal breath that vivifieth the human soul. Love is the cause of God's revelation unto man, the vital bond inherent, in accordance with the divine creation, in the realities of things. Love is the one means that ensureth true felicity both in this world and the next. Love is the light that guideth in darkness, the living link that uniteth God with man, that assureth the progress of every illumined soul.
Love is the spirit of life unto the adorned body of mankind, the establisher of true civilization in this mortal world, and the shedder of imperishable glory upon every high-aiming race and nation.

order.why: Consider love as the first effulgence.
Read love as both the source and reception of bounty.
shortened: For example, consider and observe how the bestowals of God successively descend upon mankind, how the divine effulgences ever shine upon the human world. There can be no doubt that these bestowals, these bounties, these effulgences emanate from love.

Unless love exists, the divine blessing could not descend upon any object or thing. Unless there be love, the recipient of divine effulgence could not radiate and reflect that effulgence upon other objects.
In the same way the realm of hearts and spirits is illumined and resuscitated through the shining rays of the Sun of Reality and the bounties of the love of God.

order.why: Distinguish the divine source from its human reflection.
shortened: The Love of God is like the Sun - it shines upon everything and this is His relationship to man: But the love of man to God is borrowed Light because it is impossible for Man to love unless God had first loved.
Love is the greatest Bounty of God.

order.why: Introduce the four relationships described as kinds of love. Return to the account of divine love reflected in creation. Read love toward humanity through existence and eternal life.
shortened: There are four kinds of love. The first is the love that flows from God to man; it consists of the inexhaustible graces, the Divine effulgence and heavenly illumination. Through this love the world of being receives life. Through this love man is endowed with physical existence, until, through the breath of the Holy Spirit -- this same love -- he receives eternal life and becomes the image of the Living God. This love is the origin of all the love in the world of creation.

The third is the love of God towards the Self or Identity of God. This is the transfiguration of His Beauty, the reflection of Himself in the mirror of His Creation. This is the reality of love, the Ancient Love, the Eternal Love. Through one ray of this Love all other love exists.

order.why: Place divine self-knowledge beyond contingent comprehension.
shortened: None hath known God save His holy Essence, and none hath unified God save His holy Essence.

Whosoever claimeth to know Him is an infidel, by the testimony of his own self which is contingent and temporal. And whosoever claimeth to unify Him is a polytheist, by the testimony of his own self, for association with Him is impossible, and it is impossible to attribute names and descriptions to His Essence.

order.why: Read the corresponding limit upon description.
Distinguishes God’s love within His own Self from the relation of divine and human love in creation.
Retain that theme in its devotional form.
Explore the poem’s removal of separation between lover and beloved.
shortened: That invisible Essence is established upon the throne in the unseen divine realm and plays the game of love with Its own love.
"The Friend played love with Himself in pre-existence;
Without us and without I and we."

order.why: Read the dialogue concerning beauty and the limits of mortal vision.
Consider the Divine Soul and the movement of return.
shortened: And as for "the Divine Soul" (an-nafs al-ilahiyyah), it consists of the Universal Reality which brings together all of the Divine realities of the realm of Primal Manifestation (lahutiyyah) and the eternal secrets, the outer aspect of which is the ancient light and the inner aspect is the most mighty and sublime mystery, the Primal Point from which appear all things and to which they revert, from which they originate and to which they return.

order.why: Bring the reflection toward the highest human attainment.
Connect reflected love with unity and bounty.
shortened: The more love is expressed among mankind and the stronger the power of unity, the greater will be this reflection and revelation, for the greatest bestowal of God is love. Love is the source of all the bestowals of God. Until love takes possession of the heart, no other divine bounty can be revealed in it.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the human family.
shortened: All will admit, therefore, that the divine religions are intended to be the means of true human cooperation, that they are united in the purpose of making humanity one family, for they rest upon the universal foundation of love, and love is the first effulgence of Divinity.

order.why: Consider essential love described as intrinsic to the divine reality. Explore beauty witnessed without a mirror. Read the Maiden of Love as a symbolic emergence. Keep the related burning-tree passage with its supplied citation.
shortened: And when that Hidden Essence revealed Its Essence to Its Essence and showed forth Its Self to Its Self, the Maiden of Love, which was veiled within the canopy of the Essence of Unity, arose and came forth.

For love and affection raised their banner within the Essence of the Absolute prior to the manifestation of the Essential Dispositions from the stage of Primal Unity to the stage of archetypal existence.  (And the Hidden Essence became enraptured with Its own Beauty within Itself and this became the origin of all love and yearning and the source of all affection and ardour).

order.why: Read self-sufficiency through the language of praise.
shortened: Who gave power to the hand and Who taught the ink? His grace and mercy have encompassed all and are evident as the sun. He is the Describer of Himself and the Praiser of Himself. He hath no need for mention by anyone. His is the creation and the command, and He is the Mighty, the Unconstrained.

order.why: Return to the limit of creaturely remembrance.
Retain the Báb’s account of contingent mention.
Consider the reported account of phenomena originating in love.
shortened: For God is love, and all phenomena find source and emanation in that divine current of creation. The love of God haloes all created things. Were it not for the love of God, no animate being would exist.
Third, religion must be the mainspring and source of love in the world, for religion is the revelation of the will of God, the divine fundamental of which is love.

order.why: Retain the further reported formulation with its own source status.
shortened: But, while God does not create, the first principle of God, Love, is the creative principle. Love is an outpour from God, and is pure spirit. It is one aspect of the Logos, the Holy Spirit. It is the immediate cause of the laws which govern nature, the endless verities of nature which science has uncovered.

order.why: Read love as a power that transforms the human world.
shortened: The Fire of the Love of God is like unto the lightening which strikes upon the head of nature, emasculating it of its virility and leaving it fallen on the ground - a lifeless corpse. Consequently the greatest Power in the World of existence is the "Love of God"...

order.why: Consider Ibn Arabi’s account of names and their manifestation.
Read Corbin’s interpretation as a distinct scholarly perspective.
shortened: To begin with, let us recall the hadith which all our mystics of Islam untiringly meditate, the hadith in which the Godhead reveals the secret of His passion (his pathos): 'I was a hidden Treasure and I yearned to be known. Then I created creatures in order to be known by them.'... This divine passion, this desire to reveal Himself and to know Himself in beings through being known by them, is the motive underlying an entire divine dramaturgy, and eternal cosmogony.

order.why: Compare the supplied Plotinian passages on self-directed thought.
End with the challenge to connect knowing God with loving.

questions: How does the opening account of love preceding our existence change the way we understand human worth?
What distinguishes divine self-love in these passages from the self-absorption we sometimes experience?
How do the hidden treasure and the limits of description illuminate one another?
What does First John add to the relationship between the unseen God and love practised among people?
Which habits of family or community life might give practical expression to love understood as a source of unity and growth?

neighbors.invitation: Explore creation through encounter, harmony, and complementary reflections.
Consider how the image of a perfect mirror relates knowledge to divine transcendence.

references.label: 1 · 1 John 4:7–12 · Knowing through love
references.note: The letter connects love’s divine origin with the sending of the Son and an obligation to love one another. It brings the unseen God into relation with a visible practice of mutual love. Compare that movement with the compilation’s passage from metaphysical reflection to fellowship.

subjects.displayTitle: The stations of the Manifestation: one voice, several perspectives
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh writes that when He contemplates His relationship to God He is moved to cry out that He is God, and that when He looks upon His own self He finds it coarser than clay. Both statements are true at once, and learning to hear how is the whole art of reading a Manifestation of God. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá offers more than one map: a station of unity and a station of distinction; a human nature and a divine one; or body, rational soul, and the heavenly splendour that gives life to the world. Each answers a different question, and none needs to be forced into a single diagram. The oldest help is the mirror, which lets the sun appear in full without the sun ever leaving the sky. The Qur’an holds the same tension in one breath, a messenger who is only a man and yet receives the revelation of the one God, and then turns the hearer toward righteous work [1]. The question is never only who is speaking but from which station, and what change that voice asks of the listener. From here the path leads into the Manifestation speaking in the voice of Divinity, the differences between the Manifestations, and Their relationship to God Himself.
subjects.arc: Begin with divinity expressed through self-effacement, distinguish the principal perspectives, then consider how their voices appear in scripture and human experience.

order.why: Revisit the distinction between self-regard and divine effulgence.
Open with the unexpected connection between divinity and self-effacement.
Place divine utterance beside the language of humility.
shortened: When I contemplate, O my God, the relationship that bindeth me to Thee, I am moved to proclaim to all created things "verily I am God!"; and when I consider my own self, lo, I find it coarser than clay!

order.why: Introduce unity and distinction as two perspectives.
Explore these perspectives through the sun and its mirrors.
shortened: Say: The example of what is manifested in the Messengers is like unto the sun, if ye would but perceive.

And for that Sun there are two stations of knowledge for creation: One station is that wherein all else are poor before Him, and He describeth Himself by His own Self, and considereth Himself sanctified above the suns in mirrors. In another station He characterizeth Himself as the sun in mirrors, saying "I am the First Creation, and I am Noah, and I am Abraham, and I am Moses, and I am Jesus, and I am Muhammad," and thus doth He mention all the Prophets.

order.why: Read the perfect mirror and the fullness of reflected attributes.
shortened: For the other beings have each received only a portion of that light, but the universal Manifestation of God is the mirror held before this Sun, and the latter manifests itself therein with all its perfections, attributes, signs and effects.

order.why: Retain the concise image of one sun and many rising points.
Introduce the threefold account of body, soul, and divine manifestation.
shortened: Know that, while the Manifestations of God possess infinite virtues and perfections, They occupy only three stations: The first is the material station; the second is the human station, which is that of the rational soul; and the third is that of divine manifestation and heavenly splendour.

order.why: Read its relation to the education of the world.
shortened: We stated before that the Manifestations of God have three stations: first, the material reality, which pertains to the human body; second, the individual reality, that is, the rational soul; and third, the heavenly manifestation, which consists in the divine perfections and is the source of the life of the world, the education of the souls, the guidance of the people, and the enlightenment of all creation.

order.why: Consider bodily limitations within that account.
shortened: The holy Manifestations have three stations: the corporeal station, the station of the rational soul, and the station of perfect divine manifestation and heavenly splendour. Their bodies perceive things only according to the capacity of the material world; and so it is that they have at certain times expressed physical weakness.

order.why: Retain the reported threefold explanation.
shortened: Man has two planes: the physical and the intellectual. The divine revelators have three: their physical condition, which is shared by all mankind - they eat, they sleep, they are sometimes ill, they become well again, they become fatigued, they undergo all that man can undergo; their intellectual degree and their holy reality which surrounds all beings and comprehends secrets. Their horizons enfold the universe, for they are the suns of real truth illuminating all the regions of thought, dispersing the darkness, uplifting the world of mankind and making the material world heavenly.

order.why: Read the distinction between physical birth and spiritual reality.
shortened: The Body of Christ was born of Mary of Nazareth, but the Spirit was of God. The capacities of His human body were limited but the strength of His spirit was vast, infinite, immeasurable.

order.why: Keep the concise spiritual and material distinction.
Consider the reported application to Christ and humanity.
Read sorrow in relation to the human station.
shortened: "Now is my soul troubled," in this passage 'soul' means the personality, the human nature, or body of Christ - not His spirit which was perfectly happy.  The body of Jesus was perfect - His perfect and obedient servant, naturally was sorry and grieved that this great spirit would leave it - though this body was in entire subjection and obedience.

order.why: Retain the unusual reported language with its source status.
Turn toward the universal bounty attributed to Christ.
Explore the sun and rays as another distinction of stations.
shortened: Question: "And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come."

Answer: The sanctified realities of the Manifestations of God have two spiritual stations: One is that of the state of divine manifestation, which can be compared to the orb of the sun, and the other is that of radiance and revelation, which may be likened to the divine light and perfections--the Holy Spirit.

order.why: Read the reported glass-and-light analogy.
Consider the difficulty of recognizing the hidden through the visible.
Read the water of life appearing in human form.
Preserve the Báb’s distinct enumeration and symbolic setting.
Keep the supplied passage on the station of the Word.
Attend to the changing voices of inward reality and outward temple.
Close the linked readings with service and belovedness.
Retain the brief statement of two stations.
Distinguishes the Prophets’ receiving of grace from their work of educating humanity.
Read personality sacrificed in devotion to God.
shortened: "It is the same with the Cause of God. If we would know whether this Cause is complete and in full perfect order, we must see whether all its condition or graces are complete and consistent. All Divine Manifestations give up all personal condition, considerations and graces in the Cause of God to such an extent that there is nothing judged of their personality; that is, they sacrifice their personality entirely in the world.

order.why: Explore living water and the fire of Sinai.
Consider the mirrors through which prophetic revelation appears.
Retain the Báb’s passage concerning permission and the Book.
shortened: Say: After God has ordained occultation for His Friend, ye shall be guided by His light. And from the first day when God desires to raise up the true Faith, He will permit His Friend to recite from the Book of his Lord as He pleaseth by His command. Verily He is the Mighty, the All-Wise.

order.why: Read the extended distinction of created and Creator alongside varied utterances.
shortened: Unto this subtle, this mysterious and ethereal Being He hath assigned a twofold nature: the physical, pertaining to the world of matter, and the spiritual, which is born of the substance of God Himself. He hath, moreover, conferred upon Him a double station. The first station, which is related to His innermost reality, representeth Him as One Whose voice is the voice of God Himself.
The second station is the human station, exemplified by the following verses: "I am but a man like you." "Say, praise be to my Lord! Am I more than a man, an apostle?"

order.why: End with the explanation of apparently different statements about revelation.
shortened: And if it be said that all was concealed and treasured in God's Book, and that in the manifestation of the Point of the Bayan -- may the spirit of all existence be sacrificed for Him -- the veiled meanings in the divine words emerged from behind the veil in the chambers of utterance, this is the truth in which there is no doubt. And if it be said that what was mentioned before in summary came to be explained and detailed, this is the truth in which there is no doubt. And if it be said that what appeared in this wondrous Revelation had no precedent and all is new, this saying too is correct and complete. For if God, glorified be His Name, should today speak a word that all people have spoken heretofore and shall speak hereafter, that word would still be new, were ye to reflect upon it.

questions: How can the language of self-effacement help us read a claim to divine authority?
Which questions are answered by the distinctions between unity and diversity, humanity and divinity, and body, soul, and manifestation?
What does the mirror image clarify, and where might pressing the analogy too far mislead us?
How does Qur’an 18:110 connect the messenger’s human condition with revelation and the hearer’s conduct?
How might attention to a passage’s speaker and perspective change our response to apparently conflicting statements?

neighbors.invitation: Explore why a stainless Soul is described as the means of encounter.
Consider the limits placed upon knowledge of the divine Essence.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 18:110 · Mortality and revelation
references.note: The speaker affirms a human condition while receiving revelation of the one God; the verse then calls the hearer to righteous deeds and undivided worship. Compare this conjunction with the compilation’s distinctions of station, without making the verse itself state every later distinction.

subjects.displayTitle: The stages of creation: from possibility to fulfilment
subjects.introduction: Before anything exists there is, according to the Báb and Shaykh Ahmad, an inclination toward it, then a determination, then a measure, then the joining of what was measured, and only afterwards the execution, the span of its life and the completion of its record: seven stages, named Will, Purpose, predestination, fate, permission, fixed time and the book, without which nothing in heaven or earth comes to be. Bahá’u’lláh brings the scheme home. A person can watch the same stages in a single act, from the first stirring of intent to a finished deed, and learn which matters are irrevocable and which still answer to effort. Letters, colours, elements and the four causes are drawn in as counterparts, and Shaykh Ahmad explains the whole with the measuring and building of a bed. Genesis orders creation differently, through days that end in a sanctified seventh [1], and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá reads those days as ranks of existence. Where the inquiry arrives is not mastery but detachment. From there the journey continues into the Primal Will, the question of whether God alters what He has decreed, and the arcs of descent and ascent along which every created thing travels.
subjects.arc: Establish the sevenfold vocabulary, explore its symbolic and practical explanations, compare distinct philosophical accounts, and return to responsibility and detachment.

order.why: Explore how three and seven are related through symbolic letters. Read the stages through relation to God and relation to the thing itself.
shortened: I recognize, O my God, that whenever something is related to Thee, the decree of the Will is applicable to it, and whenever it is related to itself, the decree of Purpose is established in it. When this duality is realized the decree of predestination is manifested.  After these three have descended, all seven will be generated, inasmuch as it is impossible for anything to be realized save through these seven stages. Six of them belong to the letter Wáw in connection to the limitations of things, and one of them belongeth to their manifestations in the station of the Sign of God.

order.why: Open with the seven stages named together.
Enumerates the seven stages from Will to Book and relates them to seven heavens.
Read an initial explanation of their functions. Retain the alternative vocabulary of the supplied translation.
shortened: He hath brought forth Will for the existence of essences, Purpose for the determination of quiddities, Destiny for the ordering of beings, Decree for the manifestation of meanings in essential realities, and Permission, Term, and Book for the perfection of capacities in the realm of concrete existence - that all might know, through mention of these ranks, the truth of the Manifestations of His sanctity and the signs of His uniqueness in the kingdom of names and attributes, and whatsoever God hath ordained in the knowledge of ultimate ends and purposes unto infinity in the rank of essences, until it reacheth the station of dust.

Wherefore, when the Command descended, it became seven, and thus did the Imam say: "Nothing exists, neither in earth nor in heaven, save through these seven: Will, Purpose, Destiny, Decree, Eternity, Duration, and the Book. Whoso asserteth the absence of any one of these hath verily disbelieved."

order.why: Retain the related formulation without harmonizing its sequence.
Read the hidden-treasure saying through the stages.
shortened: And verily the meaning of the tradition is similar to the meaning of the verse "all things with God are as the greater world wherein all things are manifest." God, glorified be He, wished to expound in this tradition the stages of the divine action: "I was" signifies the stage of the Primal Will; "a hidden treasure" the stage of Purpose; "hidden" the stage of Decree; "and I loved" the stage of Divine destiny; "to be known" the stage of Permission; "so I created creation" the stage of Term; "that I might be known" the stage of the Book.

order.why: Compare the interpretation of biblical days as ranks of existence.
Retain the scriptural image of successive embryonic formation.
Follow the stages into life, mind, and the heart.
Close the linked readings with the reported colour correspondences.
Consider matter, form, and combination.
shortened: And this movement hath seven aspects - they can neither be decreased nor increased, for everything hath seven aspects: the aspect of matter, the aspect of form, and the aspect of composition. When these three descended they became seven. Imam Rida (peace be upon him) said: "The Will, the Purpose, and Creation are three names with one meaning." Imam Sadiq (peace be upon him) said: "Nothing exists in earth or heaven except through these seven characteristics: through will, purpose, destiny, decree, permission, term, and book." And these seven are the completions of agent and patient within themselves; and God hath decreed that all things must operate through their causes, though He is All-Powerful.

order.why: Study existence, essence, and their connection.
shortened: After the establishment of the grades of action, there remaineth no doubt that nothing existeth apart from God save through two aspects: an existential aspect, which pointeth to the manifestation of the One Who is revealed; and an essential aspect, which indicateth the modes of servitude and the receptivity of that manifestation. When these two aspects are affirmed, the rank of Qadar -- the station of linkage between the two aspects -- becometh manifest; and after the appearance of the three, the ordinance of the four is established, for the descent of the three is impossible save through the manifestation of the four.

order.why: Follow that connection into the further four stages.
shortened: The proof that a thing cannot receive existence except through seven aspects is that which I shall now indicate through wisdom's proof: For when a thing is mentioned, it has the rank of existence, and it cannot exist except through the rank of its essence, which is the cause of accepting existence. When duality is established, the link is established. When the link is established in the station of trinity, wisdom necessitates the rule of four in the descent of the Command from the unseen realm to the visible world. Therefore, in mentioning truth, the seven are required in all ranks of existence.

order.why: Retain the Báb’s interpretation through letters and sacred figures.
shortened: Then after the station of the Hidden Alif is the rank of the Soft Alif, which is the station of Destiny and contingent geometry, expressed as the station of Beauty. Then the station of the Unjoined Alif is the rank of Decree, Implementation and Origination. Then the station of the Joined Alif is the station of the Qa'im, which is the rank of Permission. Then the station of the Letters, which is the station of the Eight Imams and is the rank of Term. Then the station of the Word, which is the station of Fatima.

order.why: Read the longer symbolic and polemical account in its own setting.
shortened: Glorified be God, the All-Knowing, Who hath fashioned things by the art of choice in a manner worthy of the wondrous lights: by the Will -- the secret of possibilities; by the Purpose -- the hidden core of existents; and by Decree -- He ordained the triune marking for the sake of the sign of delimitation.

Then did the All-Wise inform, after the establishing of the five, of the decree of the Term and the Book, that naught of the ordinances of the Gate should fall from aught of things. God appointed the Term for the sake of causes, and He exalted the Book through the establishing of effects -- so that naught of existents should escape from the Book, but that they should find it expounded in causes within this Book, and its reasons made plain in the secret of this Gate.

order.why: Compare the further diary formulation.
Keep the report on the development of signs as a distinct historical topic.
Turn toward necessary relationships and the active force that controls them.
Read the extended explanation through human action and detachment.
shortened: That which is counted among the irrevocable things cannot be changed, while other than this changes through means and deeds. The first inclination that arises in man before the appearance of means is the station of Will; the first conception of means is the station of Purpose; Destiny is the station of measure and proportion, meaning the appearance of means in measure; and Fate is the composition of what was destined.

After the appearance of Fate, the execution is witnessed, which is the same as Permission. For everything there is and has been a Term, meaning the duration of its existence. Then appears the Book, which is the station of the completeness of the thing. Praise be to God that today the Mother of Stations is manifest, and that is severance from all things and committing all affairs to Him.

order.why: Read the supplied sevenfold tradition.
Consider its dialogical explanation of will, purpose, and measure.
Explore the relation between the stages and the fixation of an event.
shortened: These seven stages are Will (mashiyyat), Purpose (iradih), predestination (qadar), fate (qada'), permission (idhn), fixed time (ajal), and the book (kitab).[1] The first stage of anything for which the "thingness" of existence is not a condition is the Will. The moment thingness is attached to it, it becometh Purpose, and this moment is accompanied by predestination. The manifestation of these three stages is fate.

order.why: Read the distinction between unseen and visible stages.
Explore verb, noun, and preposition as symbolic counterparts.
shortened: The Bab interprets "verb" as a reference to the first stage of divine Action, Will, which is the source of existence... The noun symbolizes the second stage of divine Action, Determination, which is the source of the essences of things. The preposition represents the third stage, Destiny, which unites existence and essence: "Verily, the noun is the attribute of the thing as it is in its own station....

order.why: Read the Point and the completed Book in another symbolic setting.
shortened: Praise be to God, Who made the line generated from the Primal Point manifest in the letter Ba the ornament of the seal for His name overshadowing all names, Who then split it into two by the secret hidden between the two commands [Will (mashiyah) and Purpose (Iradah)], and took one up with the other under the veil of predestination [qadar]. Thereupon, the Most Great Book was completed and all who dwell in earth and heaven became adorned therewith so that the dawning-places of affirmation, subsequent to negation, might testify to that which the tree of fate [qada'] hath testified in the luminous Spot and turn toward the Dayspring of Alteration [bada'] at the scene of sacrifice....

order.why: Study its further relations to elements and causes.
shortened: Reflect upon the stage of Purpose (iradih), which is the Eve of the Primal Adam and the Throne whereon the Will is seated in the station of the All-Merciful, and consider how God hath created it with four pillars. One pillar is the stage of fate (qada'), which is the element of fire and the manifestation of the efficient cause; its color is white due to its pure simplicity in relation to the conditions of multiplicity, dimension, and distinction.... Another pillar is the stage of permission (idhn), which is the element of air and the manifestation of the material cause; its color is yellow in relation to that which is determined... Another pillar is the stage of fixed time (ajal), which is the element of water and the manifestation of the formal cause, the eternal first Pen, and the third leaf of the divine Tree, whose essence is from the East and not the West. Its color is green, and through it the green of each thing is obtained... Another pillar is the stage of the Book (kitab), which is the element of earth and the manifestation of the final cause in the world of names and attributes. Its color is red, and through it the red in each thing is obtained, the scheme of each thing produced, and the measure of each thing determined.

order.why: Explore the account of multiplicity, possibility, and choice.
shortened: After the mode of Purpose, God hath ordained five additional modes. Among them is the stage of predestination, whose object is the design (handasa) of substances, matters, existences, natures, essences, accidents, and forms after the first causes at the root of the creative act. Multiplicities and the distinction of images from realities and essences from attributes emerge in this stage.... The condition of choosing good or evil ariseth in the third stage, which is made manifest after the conjunction of the two Commands. This is by virtue of the essence of things. The secret of the possible is only revealed in the station of predestination and the triangular figure.

order.why: Read Shaykh Ahmad’s explanation, including the example of making a bed.
shortened: The fourth is fate, which is the realization of what has been predetermined and its composition in accordance with the natural system. Predestination is like measuring the materials of a bed for length, breadth, and shape. Fate corresponds to composing them into a bed.     The fifth is execution, which is the concomitant of fate. It is the act of making something manifest, revealing the causes, and disclosing the means due to the combination within it of all the stages needed to make one cognizant of the impressions of the divine active attributes. The first four stages, therefore, are the elements of the divine Act, while the fifth is their disclosure.

order.why: Consider his distinct argument concerning knowledge and creative action.
shortened: The truth is that when the creative action is related to existence, it is the Will; when it is related to the archetype ('ayn), in other words, the species form, it is Purpose; and when it is related to the limitations of the created, that is to say, their topography (handasa)--which includes length and breadth, continuance and mortality, term of duration, and the like--it is predestination. Through the accomplishment of the act of creation and the thing itself, it is fate; and through its manifestation, the revealing of causes, and the disclosure of means, it is execution....

order.why: Compare the supplied Ibn Arabi passage without merging the accounts.
Retain the supplied colour fragment with its citation and review status.
Read the fuller reported account of colour terminology.
Compare the parallel provisional translation and its practical conclusion.
shortened: Whatever is irrevocably decreed by fate cannot be changed, but whatever remaineth potential can be changed through means and actions. The first inclination that is created in man, before the appearance of means, is the stage of the Will; the first conception of means is the stage of Purpose; predestination is the stage of scheme and dimension, that is to say, the appearance of means in proper quantity. Fate is the composition of that which hath been decreed.
To God belongeth praise this day! The foundation of all stations is manifest, and it is detachment from all things and submission to His behest. In this case, these stations themselves are unveiled.

order.why: End with the demand to consider the stages together.

questions: What becomes clearer when we distinguish an intention, its measure, its execution, and its completion?
How do the sevenfold pattern of Genesis and the schemes collected here differ in purpose and imagery?
What can we learn from the varying translations, colour correspondences, and orders without forcing them into a single scheme?
How do these passages connect necessary relationships, unrealized possibilities, and the effects of human action?
Why might reflection on the stages of creation lead toward detachment and humility rather than a sense of complete intellectual mastery?

neighbors.invitation: Examine how two aspects and their relationship become a sevenfold account.
Explore creation described as a continual bringing forth and return.

references.label: 1 · Genesis 1:1–2:3 · Order, completion, and the seventh day
references.note: Genesis orders the appearance of light, realms, and living creatures through successive days, then presents the seventh as blessed and sanctified. Compare this narrative with the collection’s interpretation of days as ranks and its seven stages of causation; the texts organize their questions in different ways.

subjects.displayTitle: Descent and ascent: the human being at the dawn
subjects.introduction: The station of the human being, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá teaches, is the end of night and the beginning of day: the last degree of darkness and the first of light, the point where the arc of descent through mineral, plant and animal meets the arc of ascent that climbs through spirit toward God. It is also a place of real freedom, for one who stands on the line between light and darkness can move in either direction, and the way back up is never a return to the same earthly condition but a creating anew. Ecclesiastes, sending the dust back to the earth and the spirit back to God who gave it, holds the two returns side by side within a single human life [1]. What makes the upward movement visible, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá suggests, is education, cooperation and reciprocity: ascent is a matter of relationships as much as of inward experience. The path runs on into the ceaseless renewal of all things, into the long story of evolution, and into the spiritual wayfaring by which a soul takes its first steps into day.
subjects.arc: Begin at the human turning point, trace the movement of creation and return, then explore spiritual progress through education and reciprocal service.

order.why: Give that turning point the image of two meeting arcs.

Distinguish bringing forth from creating anew. Read the extended discussion of ascent and reincarnation. Consider the compass image and direction of movement. Explore correspondence without recurrence of the same appearance.
shortened: However, those who have thoroughly investigated the questions of divinity know of a certainty that the material worlds terminate at the end of the arc of descent; that the station of man lies at the end of the arc of descent and the beginning of the arc of ascent, which is opposite the Supreme Centre; and that from the beginning to the end of the arc of ascent the degrees of progress are of a spiritual nature.  The arc of descent is called that of "bringing forth" and the arc of ascent that of "creating anew."  The arc of descent ends in material realities and the arc of ascent in spiritual realities.  The point of the compass in describing a circle does not reverse its motion, for this would be contrary to the natural movement and the divine order and would disrupt the regularity of the circle.

order.why: Open with the human being at the end of night and beginning of day.
shortened: Man is in the ultimate degree of materiality and the beginning of spirituality, that is, he is at the end of imperfection and the beginning of perfection. He is at the furthermost degree of darkness and the beginning of the light. That is why the station of man is said to be the end of night and the beginning of day, meaning that he encompasses all the degrees of imperfection and that he potentially possesses all the degrees of perfection. He has both an animal side and an angelic side; and the role of the educator is to so train human souls that the angelic side may overcome the animal.

order.why: Ground both movements in origin and return.
shortened: All things proceed from God and unto Him they return. He is the source of all things and in Him all things are ended.

order.why: Consider creation and return as continual.
Read the ocean and returning seas as another image.
shortened: This is the Ocean out of which all seas have proceeded, and with which every one of them will ultimately be united. From Him all the Suns have been generated, and unto Him they will all return.

order.why: Consider the common goal toward which nature yearns.
shortened: The Creator of all is One God. From this same God all creation sprang into existence, and He is the one goal, towards which everything in nature yearns.

order.why: Bring motion into both outer phenomena and consciousness.
Retain the reported account of continuous creation.
shortened: God did not create the world suddenly but God's breath of life becomes God's creative word of command, logos, which continuously creates the world. We have a continuing and not a single act of creation.
All created things, i.e. emanated things, move in a cycle, better expressed, in an elliptical curve.

The Bab and Baha'u'llah  taught: The creation, the emanated, is the descending curve of the Logos (the breath of life of God) and the development (evolution) is the ascending curve; this (curve) is, however, nothing else than the coming back or returning of all things to God, be it for destruction or for absolute perfection.

order.why: Introduce the reported diagram of two arcs. Explore the reported danger of remaining stationary.
Read the further circular illustration with its source status. Read the reported lowest point as the dawn of new life. Compare the further version of that explanation.
shortened: If we represent creation by a circle, at the top of it is God the creator, from His left descends the mineral creation, beginning first with the mineral kingdom, next below that is the vegetable kingdom, below that again is the animal kingdom, and at the bottom of the circle is man. This signifies that man has the power of being infinitely more degraded than the other three kingdoms and can do more harm.
But though this station is the "lowest of the low", it is also the dawning point of the new life, and the spiritual ascent to God!

order.why: Explore the Point unfolding into letters and returning to its centre.
shortened: Praise be to God Who created and brought forth a comprehensive, perfect, all-encompassing Point, possessing and containing all universal meanings in the world of existence, wherein all realities, effects and ordinances are integrated and included through simplicity and unity, calling to oneness in all affairs in the realm of being.

Then it became detailed, multiplied, branched out and was explained, and revolved in the circle of letters, appearing in the most wonderful forms, becoming a magnet for its spirits, and manifesting with the most beautiful beauty in all ranks and stations.
Then it returned and came back to its center in the praiseworthy station.

order.why: Retain the historical application of descent without universalizing it.
Close the linked readings with daily progress.
Consider the distinction of material night and spiritual day. Read the analogy of learning an alphabet. Read the reported account of spiritual birth and ascent.
shortened: The first or descending scale is the natural or material one.  The second or ascending scale is the spiritual.  The first half is the night the second is the day.  The world is the greatest distance from GOD, but the rays of GOD upon it are direct ones.  The world is the darkest, but it is always so before the dawn, and the ascending scale begins the day.

There are three births: first, the material; second, to be born of water; third to be born of spirit.  When man first enters the spiritual world he is born of water or the truth and knowledge of GOD.  He must become as a little child-unworldly, without jealousy, enmity, covetousness, love of money, desires, and to take on all the qualities of GOD, and begin to ascend the other half of the circle.

order.why: Read the dawn through unity and guidance.
Connect human possibility with education. Revisit that connection in the supplied parallel passage.
Consider freedom at the boundary between light and darkness.
shortened: For man standeth on the demarcation line between light and darkness. In the circle of existence, he is situated at the lowest point, which marketh at once the end of the arc of descent and the beginning of the arc of ascent. For this reason, he is free to move in either direction: towards light or darkness, towards ignorance or guidance---depending on the one that prevaileth. Should the rational faculty prevail, man would shine radiantly and occupy a lofty station in the realms on high. And should the self and the lower nature prevail, the result would be darkness and he would fall into the nethermost fire.

order.why: Distinguish material decline from the account of spiritual progress. Keep the brief statement of motion.
shortened: Everything moves forward or backward, nothing is without motion.
All material things progress to a certain point, then begin to decline. This is the law which governs the whole physical creation.

All creation, whether of the mineral, vegetable or animal kingdom, is compelled to obey the law of motion; it must either ascend or descend. But with the human soul, there is no decline. Its only movement is towards perfection; growth and progress alone constitute the motion of the soul.

order.why: Read the arcs in relation to names and attributes.
Locates the body at the opposite limits of the arcs of descent and ascent.
Return to the creative Word and a world continually renewed.
shortened: Such as communicate the generating influence and such as receive its impact are indeed created through the irresistible Word of God which is the Cause of the entire creation, while all else besides His Word are but the creatures and the effects thereof.

Every thing must needs have an origin and every building a builder. Verily, the Word of God is the Cause which hath preceded the contingent world -- a world which is adorned with the splendours of the Ancient of Days, yet is being renewed and regenerated at all times. Immeasurably exalted is the God of Wisdom Who hath raised this sublime structure.

order.why: End with cooperation and reciprocity as signs of a higher order.
Retain the supplied Qur’anic formulation of origination and return.
Read Izutsu’s account of Ibn Arabi as a distinct interpretation.
Keep the supplied image of a current returning to its source.
Introduce the supplied Plotinian language of return.
Consider its further account of a common origin and goal.
Read the biblical distinction between dust and spirit.

questions: What possibilities does the image of the human being at the dawn open for understanding education?
How do continual creation and continual progress change the meaning of a spiritual journey?
What distinguishes spiritual ascent here from returning to the same earthly condition?
How does the passage from Ecclesiastes illuminate return, and what further questions do these selections bring to it?
What would increased cooperation and reciprocity look like as evidence of spiritual growth in a community?

neighbors.invitation: Consider necessary relationships within the realities of things.
Explore love as the bond of growth and civilization.

references.label: 1 · Ecclesiastes 12:1–7 · Remembering and returning
references.note: The poem urges remembrance of the Creator before the losses of age, then distinguishes the return of dust to earth from that of spirit to God. Compare its finite human horizon with the compilation’s accounts of spiritual progress and continual renewal.

subjects.displayTitle: Creation in pairs: relationship, difference, and the creative word
subjects.introduction: Two letters, B and E, spoke the world into being, and the Báb reads in that single command a whole grammar of relationship: the Káf of the Primal Will, father of all things, and the Nún of Purpose, their mother; the word as body and the meaning as its spirit. Creation, on this account, is paired to its roots, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá praises a God who made realities through the mutual encounter of His names, like facing mirrors whose reflections complete each other. The Qur’án extends the field of pairs to the earth’s growth, to human beings, and to things beyond our knowledge [1]. The same teachings guard the image from misuse: masculine and feminine, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says, belong to bodies and have no connection with the spirit, so that Adam and Eve, are symbols of how difference participates in unity, never a ranking of persons. The thread leads onward into the Word of God as the cause of creation, into the way things are known by their opposites, and into the relativity of complementary truths.
subjects.arc: Begin with the creative command, explore word and meaning and complementary realities, then test the reach and limits of the metaphors through spirit, relationship, and humility.

order.why: Study active force and reception in the Tablet of Wisdom.
shortened: That which hath been in existence had existed before, but not in the form thou seest today. The world of existence came into being through the heat generated from the interaction between the active force and that which is its recipient. These two are the same, yet they are different. Thus doth the Great Announcement inform thee about this glorious structure. Such as communicate the generating influence and such as receive its impact are indeed created through the irresistible Word of God which is the Cause of the entire creation, while all else besides His Word are but the creatures and the effects thereof.

order.why: Open with hidden gems made manifest through the creative command.
Explore generosity and preservation through its two letters.
Read the Báb’s distinction of substance and multiplicity. Read Will and Purpose through parental and formal metaphors.
shortened: The Kaf is the rank of the Primal Will, and the Nun is the rank of Purpose, and the Primal Will is the father of all things and Purpose their mother.

Through the Kaf God created the substance of things and the sign of His uniqueness and the temple of His oneness, indicating God alone, and it is the highest consciousness in contingency wherein God alone is known, and it is called the heart. Through the Nun God created things from the beginning of inclination toward Himself to the uttermost multiplicity, from infinity unto infinity.

order.why: Bring the relationship into words and meanings.
Introduce Adam and Eve as symbolic realities.
Immediately distinguish spiritual reality from bodily sex.
Read paired creation in relation to marriage and unity.
Relates paired creation and union to divine purpose, harmony and gladness.
Retain the concise statement about mates in living nature.
Keep the reported account of affinities with its source status.
shortened: That is, were the souls created in pairs and did they belong to each other forever and ever, even if they did not meet on this earth?

He said: "Yes" - that everything was created in pairs, but that this earth was the flaming sword and sometimes, even if affinities met, they could not be happy for various reasons connected with the imperfect conditions here; but in spirit they were related forever.

order.why: Retain the historical explanation of lightning as a distinct kind of claim.
Return to the command revealed through the Beloved.
Connect remembrance with the fruits of knowledge.
shortened: O loved ones of God! Have ye forgotten the remembrance of Him at Whose command the letter K was joined with its pillar N, by Whom all faces were turned toward the face of your Lord, the Mighty, the Praised, through Whom the Tree of man yielded the fruits of divine knowledge and the oceans of understanding surged in human hearts?

order.why: Close the linked readings with a prayer for responsive action.
Retain the related Báb passage with its boundary status. Explore the treasuries between the letters. Retain the invitation to find evidence in pairs.
shortened: He it is Who createth what He willeth through His command "Be" and it is.
Say: God hath created no ink but He hath created it by His command, wherewith ye write. And God hath created of everything pairs that ye might draw inference therefrom.

order.why: Read remembrance and love through the same symbolism.
Consider the further letter correspondences.
Retain the dynamic imagery of the letters joining.
Keep the parallel statement of the worlds’ origin.
Read relation to God and to the thing itself.
shortened: I recognize, O my God, that whenever something is related to Thee, the decree of the Will is applicable to it, and whenever it is related to itself, the decree of Purpose is established in it. When this duality is realized the decree of predestination is manifested.

order.why: Explore how a duality and its link become further stages.
shortened: The proof that a thing cannot receive existence except through seven aspects is that which I shall now indicate through wisdom's proof: For when a thing is mentioned, it has the rank of existence, and it cannot exist except through the rank of its essence, which is the cause of accepting existence. When duality is established, the link is established. When the link is established in the station of trinity, wisdom necessitates the rule of four in the descent of the Command from the unseen realm to the visible world. Therefore, in mentioning truth, the seven are required in all ranks of existence.

order.why: Read paired realities through encounter and complementary reflection.
Read the warning that the term has more than one meaning.
Retain the ethereal explanation as historical natural philosophy.
shortened: "The world of existence came into being through the heat generated from the interaction between the active force and that which is its recipient." That is to say: The substance and primary matter of contingent beings is the ethereal power, which is invisible and known only through its effects, such as electricity, heat, and light--these are vibrations of that power, and this is established and proven in natural philosophy and is known as the ethereal matter. This ethereal matter is itself both the active force and its recipient; in other words, it is the sign of the Primal Will in the phenomenal world.

order.why: Compare the reported account of light and friction.
Read the supplied pairing of elements.
Retain the humoral passage in its historical vocabulary.
End with a prayer acknowledging the limits of comprehension.
shortened: How can, then, such a man succeed in befittingly extolling the One through a motion of Whose finger all the names and their kingdom were called into being, and all the attributes and their dominion were created, and Who, through yet another motion of that same finger, hath united the letters B and E (Be) and knit them together, manifesting thereby what the highest thoughts of Thy chosen ones who enjoy near access to Thee are unable to grasp, and what the profoundest wisdom of those of Thy loved ones that are wholly devoted to Thee are powerless to fathom.

order.why: Read the supplied explanation of the letters as creative power.
Consider their place in the word of command.
Read the supplied Qur’anic formulation.
Keep the supplied fragment concerning the active agent.
Explore activity, heat, and motion.
Compare the supplied Daoist account of generative relations.
Consider the Báb’s critique of identifying contingent relations with God.
Read the relation to creation through Will and command.

questions: What different kinds of relationship are suggested by words and meanings, mirrors, parents, and active and receptive forces?
How does the statement that spirit is beyond masculine and feminine qualities affect our reading of gendered symbols?
What does Qur’an 36:36 invite us to notice, and how does its reference to what we do not know encourage restraint?
How can we distinguish a metaphysical image from a historical scientific explanation while giving each a careful reading?
What might complementarity contribute to unity when it is not treated as a ranking of persons or a restriction on their capacities?

neighbors.invitation: Follow existence, essence, and their connection into the seven stages.
Consider the symbolic relation between beauty and its mirrors.

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 36:36 · Pairs known and unknown
references.note: The verse praises the creator of pairs in what the earth grows, among human beings, and in things beyond their knowledge. Compare its widening field of attention with the compilation’s many uses of pairing, while considering what each particular image can and cannot establish.

subjects.displayTitle: Knowing God: the unseen and the encounter with revelation
subjects.introduction: The Essence of God, Bahá’u’lláh teaches, is sealed away from every mind; no thought reaches it, and whoever points to it only stirs up dust. Then comes the surprise: the Unseen can be known through this Visible One. A mirror does not hold the sun, yet turned toward it the mirror blazes with the sun’s light, and so the Manifestation of God, a human temple in which all the divine names shine, is the one place where knowledge of God is truly possible. Everything else, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá warns, is the worship of an image made in the mind, a fancy worse than an idol because an idol at least exists. When Philip asks Jesus to show him the Father, the answer turns him back toward the words and works in front of him [1]. The same turning asks us to look with our own eyes rather than on another’s word. From here the way leads into the Manifestation as mediator, into the knowledge of the attributes, and into the meaning of attaining the presence of God.
subjects.arc: Begin with the visible and unseen, explore the mirror and the limits of conception, then move toward independent recognition, interpretation, and the scope of mercy.

order.why: Read the distinction between the transient and the Eternal.
shortened: And since there can be no tie of direct intercourse to bind the one true God with His creation, and no resemblance whatever can exist between the transient and the Eternal, the contingent and the Absolute, He hath ordained that in every age and dispensation a pure and stainless Soul be made manifest in the kingdoms of earth and heaven.

order.why: Open with the stark invitation to know the unseen through the visible.
Consider the Manifestation’s own person as evidence.
shortened: He Who is everlastingly hidden from the eyes of men can never be known except through His Manifestation, and His Manifestation can adduce no greater proof of the truth of His Mission than the proof of His own Person.

order.why: Develop the image of the perfect mirror.
shortened: For the other beings have each received only a portion of that light, but the universal Manifestation of God is the mirror held before this Sun, and the latter manifests itself therein with all its perfections, attributes, signs and effects.

The knowledge of the reality of the Divinity is in no wise possible, but the knowledge of the Manifestations of God is the knowledge of God, for the bounties, splendours and attributes of God are manifest in them. Thus, whoso attains to the knowledge of the Manifestations of God attains to the knowledge of God, and whoso remains heedless of them remains bereft of that knowledge.

order.why: Consider the mediating role of revelation.
shortened: As the essence of Divinity transcends the comprehension of man, therefore God brings forth certain Manifestations of the divine Reality upon Whom He bestows heavenly effulgences in order that They may be intermediaries between humanity and Himself.

order.why: Locate knowledge of divine attributes in the Manifestations.
shortened: Thus all that the human reality knows, discovers and understands of the names, attributes and perfections of God refers to these holy Manifestations and leads nowhere else: "The way is cut off, and all seeking rejected."

order.why: Keep the divine Essence beyond manifestation, ascent, and descent.
shortened: The entire world hath been created specifically for the recognition of the Ancient King, and there is no doubt that His recognition cannot be attained except through recognition of the Manifestation of His signs and the Dawning-Place of His evidences, inasmuch as the Ancient Being hath ever been and will forever continue to be sanctified, in His state of absolute transcendence and loftiest exaltation, from manifestation and appearance, from ascent and descent.

order.why: Explains why knowledge of God is attained through His Prophet and develops the chain of spiritual recognition.
Read self-knowledge through recognition in each age.
Consider the gems brought forth from the human mine.
shortened: These words have streamed from the pen of this Wronged One in one of His Tablets: "The purpose of the one true God, exalted be His glory, hath been to bring forth the Mystic Gems out of the mine of man -- they Who are the Dawning-Places of His Cause and the Repositories of the pearls of His knowledge; for, God Himself, glorified be He, is the Unseen, the One concealed and hidden from the eyes of men.

order.why: Read the extended account of the source of knowledge.
shortened: Were it not for Him, no one would have known God and none would have become aware of Him. All the knowledge of those who know, the understanding of the sincere ones, the remembrances of those near unto God, and the descriptions of those who describe, return unto this station. For the recognition of His Self is the recognition of God, His commandments are God's commandments, His utterance is God's utterance, and His word is the Word of God. Whoso turneth away from Him hath turned away from God, and whoso turneth unto Him hath turned unto God.

order.why: Retain the concise statement of recognition through the dawning-place.
Face the warning against worship of an imagined reality.
Distinguish familiar names from the one they signify.
Consider recognition tested by a new form of appearance.
Read the demanding claim concerning devotion, recognition, and service.
shortened: Should anyone today engage in the worship of all who are in the heavens and on earth, and acknowledge in his heart the Manifestations of justice, and perform with his limbs every good deed, it shall profit him not so much as a grain of mustard seed unless he enters beneath the shadow of the Divine Countenance, becomes assured of God's grace and mercy, and arises to serve God and assist His Cause to the extent of his ability.

order.why: Close the linked readings with the challenge of interpreting revelation. Read grace responding to the closed door of essential knowledge. Seek illumination concerning difficult scriptural allusions. Revisit that invitation in the presence of perplexity.
shortened: The door of the knowledge of the Ancient of Days being thus closed in the face of all beings, the Source of infinite grace, according to His saying: "His grace hath transcended all things; My grace hath encompassed them all" hath caused those luminous Gems of Holiness to appear out of the realm of the spirit, in the noble form of the human temple, and be made manifest unto all men, that they may impart unto the world the mysteries of the unchangeable Being, and tell of the subtleties of His imperishable Essence.

The knowledge of Him, Who is the Origin of all things, and attainment unto Him, are impossible save through knowledge of, and attainment unto, these luminous Beings who proceed from the Sun of Truth. By attaining, therefore, to the presence of these holy Luminaries, the "Presence of God" Himself is attained.

Those words uttered by the Luminaries of Truth must needs be pondered, and should their significance be not grasped, enlightenment should be sought from the Trustees of the depositories of Knowledge, that these may expound their meaning, and unravel their mystery. For it behooveth no man to interpret the holy words according to his own imperfect understanding, nor, having found them to be contrary to his inclination and desires, to reject and repudiate their truth.

order.why: Begin the supplied readings with investigation through one’s own eyes.
shortened: Behold thy Lord's Cause with thine own eyes, then know it through thine own self and thy spirit, for the recognition of others cannot serve as proof for thee, nor can the rejection of all else stand as evidence against thee.

order.why: Consider the message entrusted to the Manifestations.
shortened: Having barred the way that leadeth unto Thee, Thou hast, by virtue of Thine authority and through the potency of Thy will, called into being Them Who are the Manifestations of Thy Self, and hast entrusted Them with Thy message unto Thy people, and caused Them to become the Daysprings of Thine inspiration, the Exponents of Thy Revelation, the Treasuries of Thy Knowledge and the Repositories of Thy Faith, that all men may, through Them, turn their faces towards Thee, and may draw nigh unto the kingdom of Thy Revelation and the heaven of Thy grace.

order.why: Read the Báb’s account of the Sun of Truth.
Retain the account of divine names and recognition.
shortened: Unto this pointeth the saying of the Family of God: "Whoso knoweth you hath known God." And the saying of the Imam, peace be upon Him: "We are the Most Beautiful Names of God; none knoweth God save through our knowledge. Through us is God known, and through us is God worshipped. Were it not for us, God would not be known; were it not for us, God would not be worshipped."

order.why: Consider the limit of name and description.
Read recognition through the first Tajalli.
shortened: And the knowledge of the King of everlasting days can in no wise be attained save by recognizing Him Who is the Bearer of the Most Great Name. He is, in truth, the Speaker on Sinai Who is now seated upon the throne of Revelation. He is the Hidden Mystery and the Treasured Symbol. All the former and latter Books of God are adorned with His praise and extol His glory. Through Him the standard of knowledge hath been planted in the world and the ensign of the oneness of God hath been unfurled amidst all peoples. Attainment unto the Divine Presence can be realized solely by attaining His presence.

order.why: Keep the concise statement of mediation.
shortened: O thou maid-servant of God! No one hath any way to the Reality of Deity except through the Instrumentality of the Manifestation. To suppose so is a theory and not a fact.

order.why: Read the extended provisional translation on imagined and revealed reality.
shortened: We have no recourse but to turn in all matters toward that known Center, the Promised Manifestation, and the Witnessed Dawning-Place. Otherwise, we would worship an imaginary reality conceived in minds, a rejected creation, a mere fancy rather than conscious awareness in the human world - and this would be worse than idol worship, for idols at least have existence in the world of being.

As to that Divine Reality which is conceived in minds and thoughts - it is naught but illusion and fancy, for the Universal Divine Reality, sanctified above all attributes and descriptions, enters not into the realm of mind and thought such that man might conceive it.

order.why: Read the prayer’s refusal to encompass the divine mystery.
Consider meaning as inexhaustible and interpretation as a trust.
shortened: Know thou that just as thou art convinced that there is no end to His words, be likewise convinced that their meanings also have no end - but this is known only to their Interpreter and the treasurers of their mysteries.

order.why: Connect the subject with the source of learning.
Compare the reported discussion of prayer and conception.
shortened: Now all people worship an imagination, for they have created a God in the realm of imagination and him they worship. If you ask a soul, when he is praying, who art thou worshiping? He will say, God. Which God? The God of my conception. When, in truth, what he imagines is not God. Hence, all people are worshippers of imaginations and ideals. Consequently, there is no pathway or escape for man except the Holy Manifestations, for, as we said the Essence of Divinity is pure, is holy and cannot be brought into the world of ideas.

order.why: Consider praise directed toward the first Manifestation.
shortened: Since the dominions of the hearts and souls of men are completely unable to grasp the nature of the peerless Essence, it behoveth us to give praise to His First Creation, to His First Remembrance, His First Light, His First Advent, His First Revelation, His First Knowledge, His First Utterance, His First Manifestation, His First Dawning Place, His First Dayspring and His First Repository.

order.why: Read the distinction of three worlds and the path to the Prophet.
shortened: The prophets, however, maintained the existence of three worlds: the world of God, the world of the Will or the Word, and the world of created things. The Prophets, therefore, maintained that a knowledge of God is impossible.... There is, therefore, only one way to God and that is through the realization of His Manifestation or Prophet in that age.
These manifest the divine attributes and therefore by knowing them we can know God. The mystic path that the traveller should follow is therefore to the Prophet.

order.why: Consider the letter’s qualified appreciation and criticism of Emerson.
End with the explicit reminder that divine mercy is infinite.

questions: How does the mirror image allow a meaningful knowledge of God while preserving the unknowability of the divine Essence?
What distinguishes encountering a revealed attribute from treating our own conception as the whole of divine reality?
How does Philip’s question in John connect seeing and knowing with words and works?
How can examining with our own eyes coexist with seeking help from the recognized interpreters of revelation?
How should the closing statement about infinite mercy affect the way we discuss recognition and the spiritual lives of other people?

neighbors.invitation: Explore the distinction between body, rational soul, and divine manifestation.
Consider the relation between divine love and a united human family.

references.label: 1 · John 14:6–11 · Philip asks to see the Father
references.note: Jesus connects knowing and seeing him with knowing and seeing the Father, and directs attention to words and works. Compare this passage’s account of encounter with the compilation’s mirror image and its insistence that the divine Essence remains beyond human comprehension.
